item.text:
**7B.3 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**
- **Overall read:** **Mostly no.** I found solid evidence that Abiy’s government pushed some technocratic market reforms that, on paper, move state assets and regulation toward more rules-based administration. But the stronger record in 2024 is of **state power being used for regime/security purposes**, including coercive law enforcement, surveillance of critics, and a foreign-policy bargain over Berbera that exchanged access for stakes and possible recognition. I found **no strong direct evidence** tying Abiy’s own family or private business interests to specific contracts or licenses in 2024.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Ethiopia discussing selling 10% stake in Ethio Telecom via stock exchange, Abiy says | Reuters | 2024-02-20 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Ethiopia-discussing-selling-10-stake-in-Ethio-Telecom-via-stock-exchange-Abiy-says-45989643/ | The government discussed selling a minority stake in Ethio Telecom through a stock exchange, with the state retaining ownership stakes. This is indirect but real evidence of separating a major state asset from purely personal or patronage use. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| Positive | Ethiopia passes law to open banking to foreign competition | Reuters | 2024-12-17 | https://indianexpress.com/article/news-today/ethiopia-parliament-law-banking-foreign-competition-9730148/ | Parliament passed a law allowing foreign banks to operate, part of a broader opening of a tightly controlled sector. That points toward rule-based liberalization rather than private-family or clique capture. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| Positive | IMF Executive Board Approves Four-Year US$3.4 billion Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for Ethiopia | IMF | 2024-07-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr | The IMF said SOE reform would professionalize governance, improve reporting, and add government-independent directors and an independent NBE supervisor. That supports a technocratic, anti-capture reading, though it does not prove personal separation. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| Positive | Ethiopia reaches staff-level agreement on the first review of the extended credit facility | IMF | 2024-09-27 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24348-ethiopia-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-first-review-of-the-extended-credit-facility | IMF staff said the reform program was advancing well and that the exchange-rate regime had largely closed the official-parallel gap. That is consistent with a more rules-based economic track rather than ad hoc enrichment. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| Positive | The National Bank of Ethiopia announces the launch of a new monetary policy framework | National Bank of Ethiopia | 2024-07-09 | https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-national-bank-of-ethiopia-announces-the-launch-of-a-new-monetary-policy-framework/ | The central bank said it had enhanced technical capacity and moved toward a price-stability framework. This is evidence of institutionalization, not personal or family control over monetary policy. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| Negative | Landlocked Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland’s Red Sea port | Reuters | 2024-01-01 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/ | The Berbera MOU tied port access to possible naval use and possible recognition for Somaliland, plus possible stakes in state-run companies. That is strong evidence of state asset bargaining and foreign-policy leverage-seeking, not clean separation from private or political advantage. | 7B.3, 7B.1, 6B.5 |
| Negative | In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels | Reuters via EHRC | 2024-02-27 | https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/ | Reuters reported a secret committee established under Abiy’s authority that interfered in justice and ordered killings/arrests. This suggests parallel coercive governance serving regime/security interests rather than neutral state decision-making. | 7B.3, 7B.2, 6B.8 |
| Negative | Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-18 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups | HRW said security forces followed and intimidated human-rights workers to stop reporting. That is direct evidence of state coercion against truth-tellers and watchdogs, not separation of law enforcement from political protection. | 7B.3, 7B.2 |
| Negative | Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent | Amnesty International | 2024-02-19 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/ | Amnesty said emergency powers were used for warrantless arrests, movement limits, and bans on assemblies. This shows law enforcement being used to suppress dissent, which cuts against neutral governance. | 7B.3, 7B.2, 6B.8 |
| Negative | Ethiopia: Authorities Suspend Three Rights Groups | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups | HRW said Abiy praised reforms while the government kept cracking down on rights groups. That is a clear rhetoric-versus-practice gap and suggests selective state power, not clean insulation from political interests. | 7B.3, 7B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find credible 2024 reporting that directly ties Abiy Ahmed’s **family** or **private business interests** to specific public contracts, licenses, or regulatory approvals.
- The evidence is therefore mostly **indirect**: technocratic reform on one side, and coercive use of state power, state-asset bargaining, and selective suppression of scrutiny on the other.
- On this lens, the record supports **limited institutional separation in economic reform**, but **not a convincing pattern of clean separation from political/elite interests overall**.
